sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Column-header count badges (the unique-value count before 📊 and the ▶N▤ multi-row count) are now memoized per table and only recomputed when the set of visible rows actually changes. On a 4174-row, 21-column page that scan is roughly 88 000 cell-text extractions; restoring the full table after clearing a column filter measured 29% faster (12.6 s → 8.9 s). Implements PERFORMANCE.org Step 3.
The cache key is deliberately order-independent, so re-sorting a column is a cache hit: a sort changes row order and never the row set, and the counts do not depend on order.
The last four row sets are kept rather than only the most recent one, so the filter → clear → filter cycle hits on every leg instead of missing on all of them.

A scan that is superseded part-way through no longer records its partial result as the cached answer, so the columns it never reached are recomputed by the next pass instead of keeping a stale number for as long as the row set stays put.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: On multi-table pages, only the last sub-table's column-header counts were ever computed. Every sub-table scheduled its own scan but they shared one cancellation token, so each new one silently aborted the previous sub-table's scan before it wrote a single badge — leaving, for example, 1 of 423 badges filled on an artist's release-groups page. The token is now per table. Implements PERFORMANCE.org Step 22.

The Locality→Region correction applied to flag-decorated area cells (which lands up to six seconds after the render, once a third-party flag userscript has decorated them) now invalidates the affected table's cached column data. Previously the unique-values dropdown and the column-header counts could keep serving values read before the correction moved them between columns.
